subject: Using unmarkedFrameGDS to account for multiple time intervals with distance sampling

messages.author: f2621ae6892d3dbf
messages.subject: Using unmarkedFrameGDS to account for multiple time intervals with distance sampling
parts:
Hi everyone,

I think I have a pretty basic question for you all here, and I'd appreciate any help from folks with more experience than me (which isn't very much to begin with).

I've been trying to use unmarkedFrameGDS and gdistsamp to build a model that accounts for both the intervals of distance to observation and time (which consisted of three 3-minute intervals where all observed individuals were recorded, amounting to 9 continuous minutes spent at each point location). In my attempt to accomplish this, I've formatted my unmarkedFrameGDS in the following way:

umfBAHO <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y = BAHOdist, siteCovs=covs, dist.breaks=c(0, 20, 40, 80, 160),
                            unitsIn="m", survey="point", numPrimary=3)

My actual question here deals with what this frame is accomplishing. Does this division of each count into 3 time intervals accomplish anything besides multiplying my survey effort by 3? I understand that removal sampling won't apply here unless I remove re-counted individuals from each subsequent interval, and I don't think there exists any method of layering detection probabilities found with distance and time removal measurements.

I appreciate if anyone can help me think about this the correct way! I also can provide more information on my code as needed.

Michael

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Using unmarkedFrameGDS to account for multiple time intervals with distance sampling
parts:
hi  Michael, you should see the Chandler et al. (2011) paper for a detailed description of the model (below). What this model does is allow non-closure between the primary periods in the forma of a temporary emigration model.  In particular, it assumes N[I,t] ~ Bin(M[I], phi). This might be a sensible model if individuals are moving outside of a fixed-radius point count during the survey.  You'll have to read the paper and decide for yourself if that makes sense in your situation. In the Chandler et al. paper there is a nice application of a similar model (not distance sampling) to density estimation of birds.
regards
andy
